title: Opaline Systems — Inference Security & Deployment Onramp
next_steps: Send SOC 2 and ISO27001 certs and summary slide
Share Private deployment architecture doc and BOM
Schedule 60-min POC scoping with infra and SecOps next week
action_items: Maya: Email SOC2 report + high level gap doc by 2027-12-03
Devon: Prepare private deployment reference architecture and HSM integration notes by 2027-12-06
Rajesh: Share current VPC topology and list of compliance requirements by 2027-12-05
summary: Intro call to map Opaline's security constraints and decide between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private. Key asks: SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs retention, encryption with customer KMS/HSM, on-prem air-gapped possibility, and data residency. Redwood AE/SE described tradeoffs and initial path: start with Dedicated for predictable SLAs then move to Private if KMS/HSM air-gapped is required. Agreed next step — share certs and architecture and schedule POC scoping.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-12-02 09:14 PT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Torres (Redwood AE), Devon Kline (Redwood SE), Priya Anand (Redwood Solutions), Rajesh Iyer (CTO, Opaline), Sofia Martinez (Head of Platform), Evan Lu (SecOps), Marta (Legal, joined 00:18)

Summary / purpose: quick security intake to understand if Opaline can start on Redwood Hosted or needs Dedicated/Private due to KMS/HSM and strict data deletion/regulatory needs.

00:00 Rajesh: "Alright good morning everyone, thanks for squeezing us in. We're trying to map options for inference workloads — low latency for chat assistants, some batch embeddings, but security and key control is the gating item.

00:22 Maya: "Thanks Rajesh. I'll hand it off to Devon to do a quick run of how Redwood surfaces these features, and then we'll map to your constraints."

00:35 Devon: "Cool. Quick note — we'll touch on SOC2 and ISO, SSO SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, HSM, and deletion. Apologies if I bluster through some things, I might use shorthand.

00:50 Sofia: "Totally. For context: we evaluate on three axes: compliance, latency/cost, and ability to control keys. If we can't provide our own KMS or HSM, we likely need air-gapped private infra.

01:08 Devon: "Understood. Hosted (Redwood API) is the fastest — we manage keys and infra, SOC2 in place, full multi-tenant model. Dedicated means single-tenant GPUs and reserved capacity with network controls and longer retention for logs; you can get tenant isolation and better SLOs. Private is where you get the private control plane and can hook up your KMS or HSM — either cloud KMS or an on-prem HSM via a tunnel, depending on the project.

01:40 Evan: "When you say \"hook up\" to our HSM, what does that look like? We can't allow egress of key material, and our compliance team expects no plaintext key movement.

01:55 Devon: "Great question. For cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS, GCP KMS), we support customer-managed keys — Redwood never persists raw key material. For on-prem HSMs we've done a proxy/connector model: the HSM stays on your network and we route encrypt/decrypt calls over a mutual-TLS tunnel into the HSM. There's a few patterns. If you require an air-gapped setup, that's essentially Private on-prem deployment. In that case, the entire inference runtime runs in your environment and you control the HSM.

02:34 Rajesh: "Okay so Hosted is out for HSM use-case. Is Dedicated also out? I mean, can Dedicated allow a KMS integration?

02:46 Devon: "You can integrate customer-managed cloud KMS with Dedicated — that's pretty common. The difference is if you need a physical HSM on-prem, Dedicated in our cloud offering won't satisfy air-gap policies. Dedicated supports BYOK via cloud KMS and can be configured to not persist certain artifacts.

03:08 Sofia: "What about SSO — we run Okta, and we need SAML for admin access and RBAC to enforce separation between platform and app teams.

03:20 Maya: "We support SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning, fine-grained RBAC at token and route level. Devon can run through the console permissions.

03:33 Devon: "Yes. Roles map to API tokens and console roles; you can scope tokens to models, rate limits, and routes. Audit logs capture who created tokens, who rotated them, and request metadata — we can export logs to your SIEM or to S3 in your account if needed.

03:55 Evan: "How detailed are audit logs — do you log request/response bodies? Our compliance team forbids storing PII in logs.

04:10 Devon: "Default logs capture metadata: request id, caller identity, route, model, input size, latencies, error codes. We do NOT log full prompts or responses by default. For debugging we have a configurable debug trace that can capture payloads but it's opt-in and controlled, and can be routed into your destination that you manage.

04:35 Rajesh: "What's the retention — we need 3 years of immutable audit logs for our auditors.

04:43 Maya: "Short answer: Hosted standard retention is 90 days for detailed traces and 13 months for aggregated billing logs. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can extend retention and provide write-once S3 buckets or SIEM forwarding. We'll need to thread that through our support/enterprise contract.

05:05 Sofia: "OK. Another question — data deletion and data residency. Can you guarantee deletion of prompts/embeddings and how quickly?

05:20 Devon: "We have deletion APIs and data-at-rest encryption. For Hosted, customer data is deleted per the data retention policy; standard SLA is 30 days for removal from hot stores, then eventual deletion from backups within our backup lifecycle — that varies. For Dedicated and Private we can provide a deletion SLA in contract — Private is best if you need to fully control retention lifecycle because data never leaves your environment.

05:55 Evan: "Do you provide verifiable proof? Like hash-based evidence of deletion or audit logs that show purge events?

06:05 Devon: "We can provide deletion event logs and tombstone records. For higher assurance we can coordinate a joint process with your SecOps to run checksums on S3 objects or provide manifests of deleted keys. This is part of enterprise choreography.

06:22 Marta (Legal, slight echo): "On the contract side we need SOC2 and ISO certificates and a short summary of subprocessor list.

06:31 Maya: "Absolutely, we'll send the SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 cert PDFs and an appendix listing subprocessors. I'll attach a one-pager explaining what fields are in those reports so your legal team doesn't have to read the whole thing.

06:45 Rajesh: "For RBAC — can you do token scoping down to specific models or prompt types? We want our product team to only call embeddings and not gen models.

06:57 Devon: "Yes — policy language supports scoping tokens by method (embeddings/generation/prompting), model family, and route. We also support route-level quotas and per-token cost tracking.

07:10 Sofia: "Encryption in transit — mutual TLS? And do you support TLS 1.3 only?

07:18 Devon: "We enforce TLS 1.2+ with recommended TLS 1.3 for Hosted and Dedicated; mutual TLS is available for Private and for Dedicated customer connectors. For Hosted API we do bearer token over TLS — if you need mTLS we can set up a proxy/bastion.

07:40 Evan: "One more nuance: our security policy requires no third-party access to logs and a chain-of-custody for any forensic requests.

07:52 Maya: "We can make logs push to your S3/GCS/SIEM so Redwood doesn't retain a copy beyond short operational windows. For forensic requests we honor legal requests per contract and we can document the chain-of-custody process.

08:10 Rajesh: "Latency: a lot of our inference is sub-150ms p50. How do Dedicated/Private latency profiles look versus Hosted?

08:23 Devon: "Hosted nodes are pooled and optimized for overall latency; p50 can be 50-200ms depending on model and prompt length. Dedicated gives you pinned GPUs and better tail latencies. Private (on-prem) will give you the best latency if your apps are co-located. There's also a tradeoff with batching and cost.

08:47 Sofia: "We will probably test a smaller model locally for interactive chats and push larger models to Redwood. What's the approach for model variants?

08:57 Devon: "You can pin model versions and the runtime supports automatic fallback to quantized variants in case of capacity or cost-driven routing. We can whitelist models per customer.

09:10 Evan: "Does Redwood support FIPS endpoints or FIPS-compliant crypto for US Gov work?

09:18 Devon: "We have FIPS-compatible configurations for Dedicated and Private; Hosted customers can request a FIPS-enabled tenant but that's a special setup. We'll flag it for internal compliance.

09:30 Rajesh: "Who in Redwood is the SOC2 contact — like if we need a table of controls mapped to our SOC2 requirements?

09:38 Maya: "I'll include a controls matrix mapping the Redwood controls to common frameworks (SOC2/ISO/NIST). That'll be in the packet with certs.

09:45 (small cross talk)

10:05 Marta: "From legal: can you outline subprocessors, where logs are stored (region), and do you support data residency in EU?

10:15 Maya: "Yes — Hosted supports region pinning (US, EU, APAC), Dedicated can be brought into specific cloud regions, and Private is fully in your control. Subprocessors list will be included.

10:28 Sofia: "Operational question: if we start Dedicated, what's the typical RTO for failover? We need predictable SLOs during deploys.

10:38 Devon: "Dedicated SLAs are contractable — typical uptime commitments are 99.9% with runbooks for automatic fallback to a failover pool in another region. For strict MTTD/MTTR we can agree runbooks and playbooks in the SOW.

10:58 Rajesh: "What about secrets management for embeddings? We want to make sure vector database keys and indices can't be exfiltrated.

11:12 Devon: "We recommend keeping vector stores in your VPC. Redwood will only store ephemeral caches; persistent embeddings can be written to your storage. For Dedicated we can configure network egress rules so data doesn't leave your subnet.

11:30 Rajesh: "Any limitations on model weights or license agreement concerns for open models you host?

11:38 Devon: "We curate open models and validate licenses. If you bring a third-party model, we validate license compatibility and may require an attestation.

11:50 Evan: "If we want to run a POC, can we get a dedicated node for a week to run throughput and KMS integration checks?

12:00 Devon: "Yes — for POC scoping we often spin up a short Dedicated slice or a Private pilot depending on the need. POC can include KMS connector testing and audit log forwarding. We'll scope the size in the next call.

12:12 Rajesh: "Great. I think at minimum we need: SOC2+ISO artifacts, private deployment arch doc, KMS/HSM integration pattern, and a POC plan.

12:24 Maya: "Yep that's the action list. We'll send the docs and propose times for scoping meeting next week.

12:35 Marta: "One last legal ask — do you have a standard DPA with EU data residency clauses?

12:42 Maya: "We do; I'll attach the DPA redline-friendly template.

12:50 (brief silence)

13:05 Devon: "Anything else on encryption at rest or token handling?

13:12 Rajesh: "How are embeddings encrypted at rest when stored on Redwood-managed storage?

13:18 Devon: "They are encrypted with customer-managed keys if you choose that option; otherwise Redwood-managed encryption keys are used. For maximum assurance, keep embeddings in your storage and let Redwood do ephemeral caching.

13:35 Sofia: "Ok — timeline: we aim to decide within 3 weeks to start a pilot in January. Is that realistic?

13:44 Maya: "Yes, timeline looks doable. We'll prioritize sending the compliance artifacts today and schedule the POC scoping.

14:00 (Marta signs off)

14:15 Maya: "Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the packet.

14:25 Rajesh: "Thanks, appreciate it.

14:30 call ends.
